newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LOOSE CANNON GREEN LEAVES AUGUSTA WITH A BANG.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LOOSE CANNON GREEN LEAVES AUGUSTA WITH A BANG.

text.p: Augusta National's rock-hard, lightning fast greens have helped remove many of the game's biggest names from Masters contention this weekend, including defending champion Nick Faldo and Greg Norman.
But one of the lesser names to miss the cut -- Ken Green -- made the biggest noise on his way out the door.

Green, a loose cannon who has often gotten into hot water with remarks in the past, enjoyed a beer on course during his round on Friday and then later branded former champion Raymond Floyd a "a dirt ball and a cheater," according to the Augusta Chronicle.

Green, 38, who lost his PGA Tour card last year and is currently taking medication to treat depression, accepted a beer from a friend in the gallery along the 15th fairway and used it to toast his playing partner, Arnold Palmer.
"I always wanted to have a beer with Arnie on the golf course," the Chronicle quoted Green as saying before taking a swig from the cup.
PGA Tour rules prohibit players from consuming alchohol during play but the Masters is not an official tour event.
Green, who shot an embarrassing 15-over-par 87 on Thursday, posted a decent 74 on Friday and missed the cut by 12 strokes.
Afterwards he was asked by a reporter to compare Palmer to other golf legends he had played with.
Green flashed back to 1987 at Doral, when he was paired for a round with Floyd and former touring pro Bobby Boyd. He said Boyd told him that Floyd took an illegal drop.
"He's a dirt ball and a cheater," the Chronicle quoted Green as saying about the 1976 Masters champion. "Ask Bob Boyd, he can verify this."
Boyd, reached by the newspaper, would not confirm Green's comment. "I do remember (Doral), but I'd just rather not comment on that," Boyd said.

Floyd, honoured by the Georgia Golf Hall of Fame with a statue bearing his likeness on Augusta's Riverwalk this week, responded: "Ken Green? Where did he come back with that one, from 10 years ago? I think I would prefer not to say anything."
